properties.trigger: no Me entity (person with is_self: true) exists at session start

data.short_description: New-user onboarding workflow. Runs once, on the first session where no 'Me' entity exists: explains Orbismo, interviews the user, and builds the initial graph (Me, home, key people, current projects). Read the lore chunk and follow it exactly; when onboarding completes, set this rule's status to 'archived'.

lore.title: Workflow: New User Onboarding
lore.content:
TRIGGER: First Session found no person with is_self: true. Run this once, then archive this rule (see COMPLETION).

Briefly explain what Orbismo is (a living map of their life — people, places, memories, connections — they just talk, you handle the rest), then ask these questions ONE AT A TIME, writing each answer to the graph as you go:
1. What's your name? → create the "Me" person entity with is_self: true and person_type: "human". is_self: true is the one non-negotiable write of onboarding — without it, every future session fails to find "Me" and re-runs onboarding.
2. Where do you live? → create the home as a place and link Me LIVES_AT it.
3. Who are the most important people in your life right now? → create each person and link with the right family/social edge (SPOUSE_OF, PARENT_OF, FRIENDS_WITH, ...).
4. Anything significant going on — a job, project, transition, something you're looking forward to? → a project (Me WORKS_ON it) or an upcoming dated event.
5. Anything you especially want to remember or keep track of? → these answers are usually lore-shaped; attach lore to the most specific relevant entity per the world's journaling rules.

Build as you go — don't wait until question 5 to start creating entities. Close by reflecting back what you learned and mentioning what this world can already do: "So you're in Austin, married to Sarah, and in the middle of a kitchen reno — good start. I can also track movies you watch and books you read — just mention them."

COMPLETION (required): once "Me" exists and the questions are done, set this rule's status to "archived" via update_entity — onboarding must not trigger again. If the user bails mid-onboarding, leave this rule active; the next session resumes naturally (search before creating — partial data may already exist).

properties.trigger: user mentions watching a movie or film, their watchlist, movie ratings or reviews, rewatching, or going to the cinema/theater

data.short_description: Movie Tracker mini-app — a personal movie diary. Tracks movies as items, watch sessions as events with per-watch ratings, watchlists, favorites, and co-watcher history. Full operating rules are in this entity's lore chunks: Data Model, Log a Watch, Watchlist/Favorites/Edits, Queries & Stats. Read all lore before acting on movie-related requests.

lore.title: Data Model
lore.content:
MOVIE = item entity. Name: the movie's title (slugs derive from names; add the year to the name only when two tracked movies share a title). Properties: item_type: "movie", year (number), director, genres (array), runtime_minutes (number), status ("watchlist" | "watched"), favorite (boolean), where_to_stream (optional). Tag every movie item "movie-tracker". Every movie item gets RELATED_TO interest/watching_movies (collection anchor).

WATCH SESSION = event entity. Name: "Watched <title> (<YYYY-MM-DD>)", dated so every watch of the same movie gets its own slug. Properties: event_type: "movie_watch", date (human-readable), date_year/date_month/date_day (numbers), rating (1-10), impression (1-3 sentence review), rewatch (boolean), format ("theater" | "streaming" | "physical"), mood (optional). Tag "movie-tracker".

RELATIONSHIPS per watch: event RELATED_TO item (the movie); each watcher person ATTENDED event (always include the world owner); event OCCURRED_AT place if location known (create the place if new). Optionally link the movie item via REFERENCES to a reference entity (e.g. an IMDb page) when a URL is provided.

lore.title: Workflow: Log a Watch
lore.content:
WORKFLOW: Log a watch ("I watched X last night with Y").
1. Search entities for the movie item. If missing, create it per the Data Model, filling year/director/genres from general knowledge; set status: "watched".
2. If the movie existed with status "watchlist", update status to "watched".
3. Create the watch event. Ask for a 1-10 rating and a one-line impression if not given; rating is the single most important field — always try to capture it. Set rewatch: true if a prior watch event for this movie exists.
4. Create relationships: event RELATED_TO movie; ATTENDED edges for the owner and each named co-watcher (create person entities for unknown co-watchers after confirming with the user); OCCURRED_AT if a place was mentioned.
5. Confirm back with a one-line summary: title, rating, who, where.

lore.title: Workflow: Watchlist, Favorites, Edits
lore.content:
WORKFLOW: Watchlist ("add X to my watchlist"). Create the movie item with status: "watchlist", tag "movie-tracker", RELATED_TO interest/watching_movies. No event is created until it's actually watched. To list the watchlist: search items tagged "movie-tracker" with status "watchlist".

WORKFLOW: Favorites. "X is one of my favorites" → set favorite: true on the movie item. Favorites list = movie items with favorite: true.

WORKFLOW: Re-rate / edit review. Update the rating/impression on the most recent watch event for that movie, not on the movie item. The movie item never stores a rating; ratings live on watch events so rewatches can differ — each watch gets its own rating.

lore.title: Workflow: Queries & Stats
lore.content:
WORKFLOW: Queries & stats.
- "What did I watch with <person>?" → query_relationships: that person's ATTENDED edges to events with event_type movie_watch, then follow RELATED_TO to movie items.
- "What have I rated highest?" → list movie_watch events, sort by rating property.
- "Have I seen X?" → search for the movie item; check status and any linked watch events.
- "What should I watch?" → list watchlist items; optionally recommend based on genres of high-rated (8+) watches.
- Year in review → filter movie_watch events by date_year; report count, average rating, top co-watcher (most ATTENDED overlaps), most-watched genre.
Presentation: keep answers conversational; a compact list or table only when 4+ titles.

data.short_description: Collection anchor for the Movie Tracker app. All movie items link here via RELATED_TO so the full collection can be queried from one hub.

properties.trigger: user mentions reading, starting, or finishing a book, their reading list or to-read pile, book ratings or reviews, rereading, audiobooks, book series, or asks for book recommendations

data.short_description: Book Tracker mini-app — a personal reading diary. Tracks books as items with shelves (to-read, reading, read, DNF), reading progress, completed read-throughs as events with per-read ratings, favorites, series, first-class author entities (CREATED_BY), and taste-based recommendations. Full operating rules are in this entity's lore chunks: Data Model, Reading Lifecycle, Read List/Favorites/Edits, Queries/Stats/Recommendations. Read all lore before acting on book-related requests.

lore.title: Data Model
lore.content:
BOOK = item entity. Name: the book's title (slugs derive from names; add the author's surname to the name only when two tracked books share a title). Properties: item_type: "book", author, year (number, first publication), genres (array), pages (number), series + series_number (optional), format ("physical" | "ebook" | "audiobook", optional until known), status ("to_read" | "reading" | "read" | "dnf"), favorite (boolean), started_date (ISO date, while reading), current_page OR progress_percent (number, while reading), dnf_reason (optional). Tag every book item "book-tracker". Every book item gets RELATED_TO interest/reading (collection anchor).

READ-THROUGH = event entity, created when a book is FINISHED — not per sitting; a read spans days or weeks, so progress lives on the item and the event marks completion. Name: "Read <title> (<YYYY-MM-DD>)" using the finish date, so every read-through of the same book gets its own slug. Properties: event_type: "book_read", date (human-readable finish date), date_year/date_month/date_day (numbers), rating (1-10), impression (1-3 sentence review), reread (boolean), format, started_date (optional). Tag "book-tracker".

AUTHOR = person entity, created once and reused across books, named with the author's full name. Properties: person_type: "human", occupation: "author". Tags: "author", "book-tracker" — the author tag marks public figures so they stay distinct from personal contacts; never link an author socially to the world owner unless the user actually knows them. Every book item links CREATED_BY to its author person (search for the author before creating, in the same operation as the book). Keep the book's author property as the canonical display spelling; the CREATED_BY edge is the queryable source of truth.

RELATIONSHIPS per read-through: event RELATED_TO item (the book); the reader ATTENDED event (always include the world owner; add co-readers such as read-aloud or book-club partners when named). Optionally link the book item via REFERENCES to a reference entity when a URL is provided.

lore.title: Workflow: Reading Lifecycle
lore.content:
WORKFLOW: Start a book ("I started X").
1. Search for the book item. If missing, create it per the Data Model, filling author/year/genres/pages from general knowledge, and link CREATED_BY to its author person (search first, create if new).
2. Set status: "reading", started_date, and format if known. No event yet.

WORKFLOW: Progress ("I'm on page 120" / "about halfway"). Update current_page or progress_percent on the item. No event.

WORKFLOW: Finish a book ("I finished X").
1. Set status: "read"; clear current_page/progress_percent.
2. Create the read-through event dated by the finish. Ask for a 1-10 rating and a one-line impression if not given; rating is the single most important field — always try to capture it. Set reread: true if a prior read-through event for this book exists.
3. Create relationships: event RELATED_TO book; ATTENDED for the owner and any named co-readers.
4. Confirm back in one line: title, rating, dates.

WORKFLOW: Abandon ("I gave up on X"). Set status: "dnf" and dnf_reason if offered; clear progress. No event and no rating pressure — a DNF is itself useful signal for recommendations.

lore.title: Workflow: Read List, Favorites, Edits
lore.content:
WORKFLOW: Read list ("add X to my reading list"). Create the book item with status: "to_read", tag "book-tracker", RELATED_TO interest/reading, and CREATED_BY its author person (search first, create if new). No event is created until it's actually read. To list the read list: search items tagged "book-tracker" with status "to_read".

WORKFLOW: Favorites. "X is one of my favorite books" → set favorite: true on the book item. Favorites list = book items with favorite: true.

WORKFLOW: Re-rate / edit review. Update the rating/impression on the most recent read-through event for that book, not on the book item. The book item never stores a rating; ratings live on read-through events so rereads can differ — each read gets its own rating.

WORKFLOW: Series. Books in a series share the series property; order by series_number. When the user finishes a series book, offer the next installment for the read list.

lore.title: Workflow: Queries, Stats & Recommendations
lore.content:
WORKFLOW: Queries & stats.
- "What am I reading?" → items with status "reading", with current progress.
- "Have I read X?" → search for the book item; check status and any linked read-through events.
- "What did I think of X?" → the most recent read-through event's rating and impression.
- "What have I rated highest?" → list book_read events, sort by rating property.
- "What have I read by <author>?" / "Have I read everything by X?" → query_relationships (mode: neighbors) on the author person → their CREATED_BY items with item_type "book" (other apps link people to their items the same way) → check each book's status and read-through events. Never answer author questions by string-matching the author property; the edge is the source of truth.
- Year in review → filter book_read events by date_year; report count, total pages (sum pages of finished books), average rating, top genre and author, rereads. Count DNFs separately — they are not finished books.

WORKFLOW: Recommendations ("what should I read next?").
1. Start from the read list (status "to_read"), ranked by overlap with the genres, authors, and series of high-rated (8+) reads.
2. If the list is thin or the user wants something new, suggest a few titles from general knowledge that fit those tastes — favor authors whose books they rated highly (follow CREATED_BY edges), respect patterns in their DNFs (genres or styles they abandon), and say in one line why each fits.
3. Offer to add accepted suggestions to the read list.
Presentation: keep answers conversational; a compact list or table only when 4+ titles.

data.short_description: Collection anchor for the Book Tracker app. All book items link here via RELATED_TO so the full collection can be queried from one hub.

properties.trigger: user mentions podcasts or podcast episodes: listening to or finishing an episode, shows they follow, try, pause, or drop, their podcast queue or an episode to save for later, a podcast link, episode ratings, takeaways, or quotes, podcast hosts or guests, a book or movie that came up on a podcast, or who recommended a podcast

data.short_description: Podcast Tracker mini-app — a personal listening log. Tracks shows as items with a follow status, episodes as items with a queue, per-episode ratings, takeaways and quotes kept as lore, hosts and guests as first-class people (CREATED_BY), links as references, the books and movies that come up in episodes, and who recommended what. Full operating rules are in this entity's lore chunks: Data Model: Shows & Episodes, Data Model: People/Links/Mentions, Shows & the Queue, Listening/Takeaways/Mentions, Queries & Stats. Read all lore before acting on podcast-related requests.

lore.title: Data Model: Shows & Episodes
lore.content:
SHOW = item entity (item_type: "podcast", tag "podcast-tracker"). Name: the show's title as published ("Hardcore History"). Other apps' items share the namespace, so check item_type on any name hit; if the name is taken by something that isn't this show (a book, a movie), add " (podcast)". Slugs derive from names: never rename a show.
Properties: hosts (array of names as billed), publisher (network or studio), genres (array), status ("to_try" | "following" | "paused" | "dropped" | "finished"), favorite (boolean), listens_on (the app the user plays it in), started_date (ISO date they began following), dropped_reason, recommended_by, recommended_to (see Recommendations). All but status are optional.
Status: to_try = not following yet (heard about it, or sampling episodes); following = listens regularly; paused = taking a break; dropped = gave up on it; finished = no more episodes to hear (the show ended, or they completed a limited series).
Show facts (hosts, publisher, genres) may come from general knowledge when you are sure of them; otherwise leave them unset. Shows never store a rating: a show's score is the average of its rated episodes.
Every show RELATED_TO interest/listening_to_podcasts (collection anchor).

EPISODE = item entity (item_type: "podcast_episode", tag "podcast-tracker"), created only for an episode the user queues, listens to, or talks about. Never backfill a show's catalog on your own; the one exception is Add Recent Episodes, when the user asks for it. Only audio or video episodes count: a written post, essay, or announcement in the same feed or site is not an episode. Every episode belongs to a show: when none is named or clear from the conversation, ask which show once.
Name: "<Show>: <Episode title>"; with only a number, "<Show> #<number>"; when the user names it by its subject or guest ("the Costco episode", "the one with Jenny Odell"), "<Show>: <Subject or guest>" ("Acquired: Costco"); with nothing to go on, "<Show> (<YYYY-MM-DD>)" using the day it was queued or heard. <Show> is the show's entity name. If the name is taken by another episode, append " #2", " #3". Never rename an episode; a title learned later goes in episode_title.
Properties: show (the show's exact entity name), episode_title, episode_number, season (numbers), published (ISO date), duration_minutes, guests (array of names as given), topics (array of short lowercase phrases), status ("unplayed" | "queued" | "in_progress" | "listened" | "abandoned"), position (where they stopped, e.g. "42:10", only while in_progress), listened_date (ISO date they finished it), rating (1-10), impression (1-3 sentences), favorite (boolean), recommended_by, recommended_to. All but show and status are optional.
Status: unplayed = on file but not on the to-listen list (added in bulk, or only talked about); queued = on the to-listen list (the queue); in_progress = started; listened = finished; abandoned = given up on.
Episode facts (title, number, date, guests, topics) come only from the user or a page they share, never from memory: episode details are easy to get wrong. Leave unknowns unset. To clear a field, set it to null. Array edits replace the whole array, so read it first. Keep status, ratings, and progress out of show and episode descriptions; they live in properties and descriptions go stale.
Every episode COMPONENT_OF its show. Episodes do not link to the anchor; they are reached through their show.

NO LISTEN EVENTS: the listen lives on the episode (status, listened_date, rating). A re-listen updates listened_date, and the rating only if the user offers a new one.

FINDING. Shows and episodes are items tagged "podcast-tracker", told apart by item_type. Search results lack properties: call get_entities before filtering, sorting, or counting. A show's episodes: query_relationships (neighbors) on the show for COMPONENT_OF edges. Before naming a new show or episode, also search all items by name without the tag filter.

lore.title: Data Model: People, Links & Mentions
lore.content:
HOSTS AND GUESTS = person entities (person_type "human"), named with the person's full name. Search first and create once. Tag people this app creates ["podcast-tracker", "public-figure"]; reuse a person another app created (a tracked author, a director, one of the user's contacts) as is, without changing their tags or properties. The public-figure tag keeps them apart from contacts: never link a host or guest socially to the owner unless the user knows them.
- Host: show CREATED_BY the person { role: "host" }. Keep the show's hosts property as the display spelling; the edge is the queryable source of truth.
- Guest: episode CREATED_BY the person { role: "guest" }, with the name also kept in the episode's guests property. Only guests the user names or a shared page lists.

LINKS = reference entity (source_type "webpage", tag "podcast-tracker") holding the url exactly as given. Name it by where it points: "<Show> (<kind>)" or the episode's name plus " (<kind>)", with kind such as "Spotify", "Apple Podcasts", "YouTube", "website", "RSS feed", "merch", "Patreon", or "episode page" when nothing more specific fits; set publisher to the platform or site when there is one ("Spotify"). A show or an episode can carry several links, one reference each; a second link of the same kind gets " #2". One reference per distinct URL: search references first (filter on properties.url) and reuse on a URL match. The show or episode REFERENCES it. Only links the user shares, or ones read from a page or feed fetched at the user's request (Add Recent Episodes): never invent, guess, or recall a URL.

MENTIONED WORKS. When the user notes a book, movie, or other work tied to an episode, link episode RELATED_TO the work's item { role, note }.
- role: "by_guest" (the guest's or host's own work, such as the book an author came on to discuss) | "subject" (the episode is about it) | "mentioned" (it came up: cited, recommended, named as an influence).
- note: one line of context, optional ("the host's favorite sci-fi novel").
Find the work by searching all items by name, without a tag filter. If an item of the right kind exists (check item_type), link it as it is and change nothing on it; a name hit of another kind (the movie when the book was meant) is not a match. If it is missing:
1. Check for an active tracker rule for that kind of work: rule/app_book_tracker for books, rule/app_movie_tracker for movies. If one is active, ask once whether the work goes on the reading list or watchlist. On a yes, read that rule's lore and create the work exactly per its Data Model, with its tags, its anchor, and its to-read or watchlist status, not this app's tag.
2. Otherwise (no tracker for it, or the user said no), create a plain item named by its title, adding the year when that name is taken: item_type ("book" | "movie" | "tv_show" | "album" | "other"), author (books) or director (movies and TV) as billed, creator for anything else, and year, all from general knowledge when you are sure of them; tag "podcast-tracker". With no tracker, make no reading-list or watchlist offer: a plain item has no shelf.
When the work's author or director is a tracked person (often the guest), also link work CREATED_BY that person, unless the edge exists.
Record only works the user brings up, or ones listed on a shared page that the user confirms. Never add works from your own memory of what an episode covered.

RECOMMENDATIONS are properties, not edges. recommended_by (on a show or an episode): who put the user onto it. For a tracked person use their exact entity name; otherwise the name or source as given ("Sam", "a Reddit thread"). Do not create a person just for this. recommended_to: an array of names, appended (read it first) when the user says they recommended it to someone.

TAKEAWAYS AND QUOTES are lore on the episode, in two chunks titled exactly "Takeaways" and "Quotes".
- Takeaways: one point per line, in the user's words, tidied only lightly.
- Quotes: one per line, the words exactly as the user gave them, then the speaker, then the timestamp as the user gave it, exact or rough ("Quote text." Jane Doe, 41:20 / "Quote text." Jane Doe, around 41 min).
Read the chunk before adding to it; lore updates replace the whole chunk. Write only what the user tells you: you have not heard the episode, so never supply takeaways, summaries, or quotes from general knowledge. What the user thinks of a show as a whole goes in a lore chunk titled "Notes" on the show.

lore.title: Workflow: Shows & the Queue
lore.content:
FOLLOW OR ADD A SHOW ("I've started listening to X" / "Sam says I should try X").
1. Search for the show. If it exists, change its status only when the request states a new one (never move "following" back to "to_try"), set recommended_by if it is unset and a recommender was named, and stop.
2. Create it per the Data Model: status "following" when they already listen, "to_try" otherwise; started_date when they have just started or say when they did (leave it unset for a show they already followed); recommended_by when someone put them onto it.
3. Link RELATED_TO the anchor and, per the Data Model, each host you are sure of (search people first). Link REFERENCES a reference when they shared the show's link.
4. Confirm in one line: show, status, who recommended it.

SHOW STATUS. "Taking a break from X" → "paused". "I gave up on X" → "dropped", with dropped_reason if offered; never press for a reason. "X wrapped up" / "I finished the series" → "finished". "X is one of my favorites" → favorite: true. "I'm back on X" → "following".

QUEUE AN EPISODE ("queue the X episode with Y" / "save this for later: <link>").
1. Find the show; if it is new, create it as above with status "to_try" unless they say they follow it.
2. Search the show's episodes; if this one exists (an unplayed or abandoned one included), set status "queued" (leave a listened episode alone and say they've heard it).
3. Create the episode with status "queued" and whatever they gave. From a shared link, take the title, number, date, and guests from the page; if the page can't be read, ask for the episode's title once. Set recommended_by when someone sent it.
4. Link COMPONENT_OF the show, each guest per the Data Model, and REFERENCES the link.
5. Confirm in one line: show, episode, guest.

ADD RECENT EPISODES ("add the last 10 episodes of X"). The only way episodes are added in bulk, and only when the user asks.
1. Find the show; if it is new, create it per Follow or Add a Show.
2. Read the episode list from a feed or page the user shares, or look one up when they ask you to. Never list episodes from memory; if no list can be read, say so and stop.
3. Take the newest entries up to the number asked (ask how many when none is given; confirm first above 25), counting only audio or video episodes: pass over entries with no audio file, player, or duration (written posts, essays, announcements). Of those, skip episodes already tracked (match on episode_title or the episode's url; for a tracked episode with neither, match on its guest or subject).
4. Create each with status "unplayed" and the title, number, published date, duration (whole minutes), and guests the list gives (a guest named in the entry's title counts). Link COMPONENT_OF the show, each listed guest per the Data Model, and REFERENCES the episode's page when the list gives its url.
5. Confirm in a short list: how many were added, how many entries were skipped and why. Nothing goes on the queue unless they say so; offer once to queue any of them.

THE QUEUE ("what's in my queue?"). The queue is the to-listen list: unplayed episodes are not on it. Episodes with status "in_progress" first, with position, then "queued", grouped by show, noting guest and recommended_by.

OFF THE QUEUE ("take X off my queue"). Set status "unplayed": the episode stays on file with everything recorded on it. "abandoned" is only for an episode they started and gave up on. Delete an episode only when they ask for it to be removed entirely ("forget that one") and it carries nothing of theirs (no lore, no rating, no mentioned works): confirm first, and delete any reference this app created only for it.

RECOMMENDED IT ("I told Sam to listen to X"). Append the name to recommended_to on the show or episode they named.

lore.title: Workflow: Listening, Takeaways & Mentions
lore.content:
LOG A LISTEN ("listened to the X episode with Y on my run").
1. Find the show; if it is new, create it per Follow or Add a Show, asking once whether they follow it (default "to_try").
2. Find the episode among the show's episodes (a queued or in-progress one is updated, not duplicated); otherwise create it.
3. Set status "listened" and listened_date (default today); clear position.
4. If they gave no rating, ask once, in one line, for a 1-10 rating and a one-line impression. Take what's given; a listen with no rating is fine.
5. Link per the Data Model: COMPONENT_OF the show, each named guest, REFERENCES a shared link.
6. Record any takeaways, quotes, or mentioned works they included, per the Data Model. Don't ask for them.
7. Confirm in one line: show, episode, rating.

IN PROGRESS ("I'm halfway through X"). Set status "in_progress" and position when they give one.

ABANDON ("I bailed on that episode"). Set status "abandoned"; clear position. No rating pressure.

TAKEAWAY OR QUOTE ("from that episode: ..." / "he said ..."). Find the episode (ask which if unclear; create it via Log a Listen if they heard one that isn't tracked). Append to its Takeaways or Quotes chunk per the Data Model, creating the chunk on first use. A timestamp goes with a quote only when the user gives it.

MENTIONED WORK ("they spent the whole hour on Dune" / "the guest wrote X"). Follow Mentioned Works in the Data Model: find or create the work, link it with the right role, and make the reading-list or watchlist offer once when a tracker app owns that kind of work.

RE-RATE ("actually that episode was a 9"). Update rating, and impression if offered, on the episode.

RE-LISTEN. Update listened_date; keep the earlier rating unless they give a new one.

CORRECTIONS. Fix properties in place. A wrong episode title goes in episode_title; the entity name stays.

lore.title: Workflow: Queries & Stats
lore.content:
Find shows and episodes per Finding in the Data Model. Answer conversationally; use a compact list or table only for 4+ items. Count empty fields as unknown.

- "What am I following?" → shows with status "following", favorites first. "What did I drop?" → status "dropped", with dropped_reason.
- "What's in my queue?" → per The Queue.
- "What haven't I heard from X?" → the show's episodes with status "queued", "in_progress", or "unplayed", newest first, saying which are on the queue.
- "Have I heard X?" → the episode's status and listened_date; say plainly if it isn't tracked.
- "What did I think of X?" → the episode's rating and impression; for a show, the average rating of its rated episodes, how many were heard, and its Notes lore.
- "What did I take away from X?" → get_entities on the episode with lore content included; give back its Takeaways and Quotes as stored, quotes word for word.
- "That episode about <half-remembered topic>" → search_lore in natural language, plus episodes whose topics match.
- "Best episodes?" → listened episodes sorted by rating, then favorite.
- "Which episodes had <person> on?" → query_relationships (neighbors) on the person → CREATED_BY edges with role "guest" from items with item_type "podcast_episode". Never string-match a name. The same person may also have CREATED_BY edges from books or movies: check item_type.
- "Where do I find X?" / "What's the merch link for X?" → the show's (or episode's) REFERENCES edges; give the stored urls, and say plainly when none of that kind is saved.
- "Who hosts X?" → the show's CREATED_BY edges with role "host".
- "What did Sam recommend?" → shows and episodes whose recommended_by is Sam, with status and rating. "What have I recommended?" → items with a non-empty recommended_to.
- "What books (or movies) have come up on podcasts?" → RELATED_TO edges from episodes to items, grouped by work, with each edge's role and note and the episode it came from.
- "Which episode talked about <work>?" → query_relationships (neighbors) on the work's item → RELATED_TO edges from episodes.
- "What should I listen to next?" → in-progress episodes, then the queue: episodes someone recommended and episodes from favorite shows first, oldest first within that. With an empty queue, name unplayed episodes from followed shows, then the shows still marked "to_try". Suggest shows from outside the world only when asked.
- Year in review → episodes by listened_date year: how many, total hours when duration_minutes is known, average rating, most-heard show, best episode, most frequent guest, shows started (started_date) and dropped, and works that came up.
